fields.help: Name of the aircraft preset this configuration started from, or blank for one built from defaults.
Design cruise Mach number: the primary speed target the optimizer sizes the aircraft around.
fields.label: Cruise Mach number

fields.help: Design cruise altitude, used to compute air density/speed of sound for the cruise design point.
fields.label: Cruise altitude

fields.help: Optional requirement: the initial cruise level a jet must reach with a 300 ft/min residual climb at maximum-climb thrust. Empty: the achievable ICA is only reported.
fields.label: Required initial cruise altitude (ICA)

fields.help: Brake-release mass the required initial cruise altitude is stated at. Empty: the maximum take-off weight.
fields.label: ICA mass basis

fields.help: Target maximum take-off weight: anchors the whole weight & balance / sizing pipeline.
fields.label: Max take-off weight (MTOW)

fields.help: 'passenger' or 'cargo': switches which cabin-preset list and payload model apply.
fields.label: Aircraft type

fields.help: Named seating/payload layout preset (passenger: high-density, two-class, three-class; cargo: max or dense payload).
fields.label: Cabin preset

fields.help: Target passenger count (if aircraft_type is 'passenger'). Auto-recomputed when a cabin preset is active, only editable with cabin_preset set to 'Custom'.
Target cargo payload capacity (if aircraft_type is 'cargo'). Auto-recomputed when a cabin preset is active, only editable with cabin_preset set to 'Custom'.
fields.label: Cargo payload capacity

fields.help: Cargo payload mass requested of a freighter, which the search is rewarded for approaching [kg].
fields.label: Cargo capacity objective

fields.help: Maximum structural payload (MZFW - OEW) [kg].
fields.label: Max structural payload

fields.help: Hard floor on the geometry-resolved passenger capacity: a candidate with fewer seats is infeasible. 0 disables it (default).
fields.label: Minimum passenger capacity

fields.help: Structural screening input for the Torenbeek mass formulas (ultimate load factor, dimensionless).
fields.label: Ultimate load factor (n_ult)

fields.help: Derive the ultimate load factor from the design MTOW by CS 25.337(b) and CS 25.303. Off uses the declared ultimate load factor.
fields.label: Load factor from MTOW (CS 25.337(b))

fields.help: Structural screening dive speed for the Torenbeek mass formulas and the V-n diagram.
fields.label: Design dive speed (V_dive)

fields.help: Negative V-n screening load factor (dimensionless). The shipped -1.0 follows the large-aeroplane CS-25 case up to VC; the positive limit is ultimate_load_factor / 1.5.
fields.label: Limit load factor, negative (n_lim,neg)

fields.help: Upper bound on the wing planform projected onto the aircraft XY reference plane; the optimizer is penalised for exceeding it.
fields.label: Maximum wing area

fields.help: Lower bound on wing loading (MTOW / wing area): keeps the wing from being sized too large for the mass it carries.
fields.label: Minimum wing loading (MTOW/S)

fields.help: Candidate designs whose required cruise CL exceeds this are rejected as infeasible (too close to stall).
fields.label: Maximum cruise CL (stall guard)

fields.help: Preferred static margin at the aerodynamic aft CG limit (fraction of MAC): aft limit [%MAC] = neutral point - target*100.
fields.label: Target static margin

fields.help: Width of the CG envelope. Forward CG Limit (%MAC) = Aft CG Limit (%MAC) - cg_range_pct_mac.
fields.label: CG envelope width

fields.help: Minimum static margin at the actual mass-model CG (fraction of MAC).
fields.label: Minimum physical static margin

fields.help: Combined average mass per occupant, body plus baggage [kg]. The shipped 100 kg is a project load-case default, not an FAA AC 120-27F figure.
fields.label: Mass per passenger

fields.help: Standard gravity, used to turn every mass in the sizing into a weight. Configuration rather than a constant so a run's assumptions are all in one place and all visible.
fields.label: Gravitational acceleration

fields.help: Fuselage-station X of the wing-root leading-edge datum: how far aft of the nose the wing sits.
fields.label: Wing root X position

fields.help: Vertical (Z) placement of the wing-root leading edge relative to the fuselage centerline.
fields.label: Wing root vertical offset

fields.help: Vertical placement of the mid-span 'break' section leading edge, where the taper/dihedral rate changes.
fields.label: Wing break vertical offset

fields.help: Vertical placement of the wing-tip leading edge. Tip above root gives positive dihedral.
fields.label: Wing tip vertical offset

fields.help: Rise of the wing tip from the static ground shape to the 1 g flight shape, as a fraction of semispan.
fields.label: Wing tip rise in flight

fields.help: Optional rise of the wing-root height from the static ground shape to the 1 g flight shape [m]; the flight height polyline starts at the raised root.
When set, nacelles hang from the static ground-shape wing in the flight shape too, as manufacturer front views draw them, instead of rising with the wing.
Geometric twist (incidence) of the root section, positive = leading-edge-up (washin).
fields.label: Wing root twist

fields.help: Geometric twist of the mid-span break section.
fields.label: Wing break twist

fields.help: Spanwise position of the trailing-edge break, as a fraction of the semispan (0 = root, 1 = tip).
fields.label: Wing break span location

fields.help: Optional fuselage side-of-body station as a semispan fraction. Leave unset to retain the legacy centerline-root planform.
fields.label: Wing side-of-body span location

fields.help: Optional side-of-body chord divided by root chord. A value near one retains wing-box and high-lift depth inboard.
fields.label: Wing side-of-body chord ratio

fields.help: Optional Yehudi-kink station as a semispan fraction. When unset, the legacy wing break span location remains active.
fields.label: Wing kink span location

fields.help: How many degrees less swept the outboard panel is than the inboard panel (a common yehudi/crank shape).
fields.label: Outboard sweep reduction

fields.help: Legacy reference-replay override. Product transport wings use the design-vector sweep across both panels so this value cannot create an unintended leading-edge crank.
fields.label: Outboard leading-edge sweep

fields.help: Optional leading-edge sweep of the inboard panel (centreline to kink) [deg]. Unset runs the design-vector sweep straight to the tip.
Optional chord at the extreme tip of a swept-back tip [m].
Optional span fraction where a swept-back tip begins (used with the rake tip chord).
Optional span fraction of an outboard trailing-edge break between kink and tip (with the break chord offset).
Optional extra chord at the outboard trailing-edge break [m], added to the straight kink-to-tip chord (positive moves the trailing edge aft).
Optional span fraction of a second outboard trailing-edge break, outboard of the first and inboard of the tip rake (with its chord offset).
Optional extra chord at the second outboard trailing-edge break [m], added to the straight kink-to-tip chord (positive moves the trailing edge aft).
Optional stations that offset the drawn leading and trailing edges from their straight lines: an inboard trailing-edge break, a leading-edge fillet, a curved raked tip.
Reference-wing convention: Drawn quotes S_ref, b_ref and MAC on the drawn planform; Trapezoid on the manufacturer reference trapezoid.
Optional wingtip device (winglet, sharklet or tip fence) added as an extra lifting surface at the wing tip.
Optional interior stations that bend the root-break-tip height polyline: dihedral that varies along the span (see WingDihedralStation).
Optional stations scaling the section thickness along the span so a thick root falls to a thin outer wing (see WingThicknessStation).
Optional interior stations naming the wing section at each; the loft blends between them, with the root and tip airfoils at the ends (see WingSectionStation).
Interpolation of the spanwise dihedral, twist and thickness profiles: piecewise linear, or a C2 cubic spline through every station.
Reference airfoil at the wing root, morphed by the design vector's thickness/camber scale factors.
fields.label: Root airfoil section

fields.help: Reference airfoil at the wing tip.
fields.label: Tip airfoil section

fields.help: Declared section technology of the main wing (conventional or supercritical), fixing the Korn factor: 0.87 conventional, 0.95 supercritical (Mason).
Optional Korn technology factor overriding the section class value (0.87 conventional, 0.95 supercritical); valid 0.80-1.00. Needs a documented section-technology source.
Relation giving the wing drag-divergence Mach number: auto follows the section class, korn is Korn's relation, torenbeek1048 is Torenbeek's Eq. 10.48.
fields.label: Drag-divergence law

fields.help: Additional validated wing sections supplied by the user; edited by the custom-geometry editor rather than the generated scalar form.
Spanwise vortex-lattice panels across the whole wing semispan, as an absolute count. Every planform station stays a panel edge.
fields.label: Wing VLM panel count

fields.help: Reference airfoil shared by both the horizontal and vertical stabilisers (usually symmetric, e.g. NACA 00xx).
fields.label: Tail airfoil section

fields.help: Optional section of the vertical stabiliser; empty builds it from the tail airfoil section. The dorsal fillet stays a flat plate.
fields.label: Fin airfoil section

fields.help: Spanwise vortex-lattice panels across each tail surface, as an absolute count rather than per section, so a later cranked fin gets the same density.
fields.label: Tail VLM panel count

fields.help: How far forward of the fuselage tail tip the horizontal-stabiliser root leading edge sits.
fields.label: H-stab offset forward of tail tip

fields.help: Vertical placement of the horizontal stabiliser relative to the fuselage centerline.
fields.label: H-stab vertical offset

fields.help: Chord of the horizontal-stabiliser root section, before the design vector's tail scale is applied.
fields.label: H-stab root chord

fields.help: Chord of the horizontal-stabiliser tip section, before the design vector's tail scale is applied. Shorter than the root chord gives a tapered surface.
fields.label: H-stab tip chord

fields.help: Incidence of the horizontal stabiliser root, usually slightly negative to trim the wing's nose-down pitching moment.
fields.label: H-stab root twist

fields.help: Incidence of the horizontal stabiliser tip. Equal to the root incidence gives an untwisted surface, which is what a trimming tail normally has.
fields.label: H-stab tip twist

fields.help: Position of the horizontal-stabiliser tip leading edge relative to its root, as (x, y, z).
fields.label: H-stab tip leading edge (x, y, z)

fields.help: How far forward of the fuselage tail tip the vertical-stabiliser root leading edge sits.
fields.label: V-stab offset forward of tail tip

fields.help: Vertical placement of the fin root line relative to the fuselage centreline [m], usually the fuselage top line at the fin.
fields.label: V-stab vertical offset

fields.help: Chord of the vertical-stabiliser root section, before the design vector's tail scale is applied.
fields.label: V-stab root chord

fields.help: Chord of the vertical-stabiliser tip section, before the design vector's tail scale is applied.
fields.label: V-stab tip chord

fields.help: Position of the vertical-stabiliser tip leading edge relative to its root, as (x, y, z).
fields.label: V-stab tip leading edge (x, y, z)

fields.help: Absolute position of the fin leading edge on its root line, measured aft from the nose tip [m].
fields.label: V-stab root leading edge x (from nose)

fields.help: Absolute position of the horizontal-stabiliser leading edge at its root, measured aft from the nose tip [m].
fields.label: H-stab root leading edge x (from nose)

fields.help: Distance from the centreline of the station where tailplane root chord, incidence, offset and leading edge x are drawn [m] (the fuselage side).
fields.label: H-stab drawn root station y

fields.help: How far ahead of the fin root leading edge the dorsal fillet leaves the top of the body [m].
fields.label: Dorsal fin length ahead of fin

fields.help: Height above the fin root line at which the dorsal fillet meets the fin leading edge. Needs the dorsal length too; leave both unset for a fin without a dorsal.
fields.label: Dorsal fin height

fields.help: How full the dorsal fillet's side line is, between 0 and 1: near 0 a straight line from the body to the fin, 0.3 when unset.
Height above the top of the body at which the dorsal fillet's side line starts, for a line that comes out from behind a nacelle [m]. Unset starts on the body.

Add the dorsal fillet to the vortex lattice as a lifting surface. Off, the fillet is part of the geometry, wetted area and drag build-up but carries no lift: test data show no effect on the fin lift curve up to 15 deg of sideslip.
fields.label: Dorsal fin in aerodynamic model

fields.help: Optional drawn stations of a ventral fin pair under the tail. Part of the geometry, wetted area, drag build-up and paint; outside the vortex lattice.
Optional stations that offset the built tailplane edges from their straight lines: a rounded tip corner. The straight-edged trapezoid stays the reference planform.
Optional stations that offset the built fin edges from their straight lines: a rounded tip corner, a cap sloping down aft. The straight-edged trapezoid stays the reference planform.
Optional stations scaling the fin section thickness from root to tip, for a fin that thins toward its tip. Chords and areas do not change.
Optional end of the fin's reference planform, as a fraction of its straight lines with 1 at the tip. Unset, a T-tail's reference fin ends at the tailplane seat.
Maximum fuselage cross-sectional diameter: the main driver of cabin width and wetted area. Best judged on the 3-view preview's front/isometric panels, not the top view.
fields.label: Fuselage diameter (width)

fields.help: Vertical cross-section dimension. Leave blank/none for a circular fuselage where height equals diameter.
fields.label: Fuselage height (if non-circular)

fields.help: Vertical offset of the nose tip relative to the fuselage centerline.
fields.label: Nose vertical offset

fields.help: X-station where the fuselage first reaches full diameter, i.e. the end of the nose taper.
fields.label: Cabin start X position

fields.help: Vertical offset of the cylindrical cabin section relative to the fuselage centerline.
fields.label: Cabin vertical offset

fields.help: Length of the aft taper, from the end of the cylindrical cabin section to the tail tip.
fields.label: Tailcone length

fields.help: Vertical offset of the upswept tail tip (positive = tail rises above centerline, typical for ground clearance/rotation).
fields.label: Tail vertical offset

fields.help: Distance ahead of the tail tip where the lower fuselage line starts rising straight to the tail tip [m]; sets the tail-strike angle. Unset keeps the tailcone law.
fields.label: Belly upsweep length

fields.help: Side-view angle of the straight windshield to the waterline [deg].
fields.label: Nose windshield angle

fields.help: Fraction of the nose length at which the upper line reaches the cabin crown with zero slope (dimensionless).
fields.label: Nose crown end

fields.help: Fraction of the nose length occupied by the radome, from the tip to the windshield base. Unset takes a narrow-body class estimate (about 0.3). Valid 0.1 to 0.45.
fields.label: Nose radome length

fields.help: Exponent of the lower nose line from tip to cabin keel (dimensionless): larger gives a deeper chin radome.
fields.label: Nose keel exponent

fields.help: Exponent of the plan-view half-width from the tip to the cabin width: smaller values give a pointier plan view. Unset takes a narrow-body class estimate (about 2). Valid 1 to 2.6.
fields.label: Nose plan exponent

fields.help: Peak superellipse exponent of the nose cross-sections (dimensionless), reached mid-nose; larger gives flatter cockpit sides. Unset about 2.4. Valid 2-3.5.
fields.label: Nose section exponent

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip at which the lofted body reaches full section [m], read from the drawing. Unset takes the cabin start X.
fields.label: Nose loft length

fields.help: Full width of the finite closing section at the tail end (APU exhaust or tail-cone cap) instead of a point [m]. Unset closes to a point.
fields.label: Tail end width

fields.help: Full height of the finite closing section at the tail end, centred on the tail vertical offset. Unset closes the body to a point, the tailcone law.
fields.label: Tail end height

fields.help: Vertical offset of the closing section centre at the tail end relative to the fuselage centreline [m].
fields.label: Tail end vertical offset

fields.help: Exponent of the belly line rising to the tail end (dimensionless): 1 is a straight ramp, larger starts gently and steepens. Unset takes 1. Valid 1-3.
fields.label: Belly upsweep exponent

fields.help: Length of the main-gear sponsons of a high wing. Not drawn on the built body: it only adds their wetted area to the parasite drag. Unset for a body without sponsons.
fields.label: Gear sponson length

fields.help: Largest half width over the main-gear sponsons, from the centreline. Not drawn on the built body.
fields.label: Gear sponson half width

fields.help: Depth of the main-gear sponsons below the keel of the body. Not drawn on the built body.
fields.label: Gear sponson depth

fields.help: Length of the plan-view (width) taper ahead of the tail end. Unset takes the tailcone length. Real aft bodies narrow in plan well ahead of the crown line dropping.
fields.label: Aft plan taper length

fields.help: Exponent of the plan-view half-width taper (dimensionless): 1 is a straight cone, larger keeps the width longer. Unset takes 1.5. Valid 1-3.
fields.label: Aft plan taper exponent

fields.help: Length of the crown (upper line) drop ahead of the tail end [m]. Unset takes the tailcone length.
fields.label: Aft crown drop length

fields.help: Exponent of the crown drop (dimensionless): 1 is straight, larger keeps the crown level longer. Unset takes 1.5. Valid 1-3.
fields.label: Aft crown drop exponent

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip up to which the loadable interior (hold, ramp floor) keeps the full cabin keel [m].
fields.label: Hold interior end

fields.help: Rise of the crown above the main crown over the full-height part of an upper-deck hump (Boeing 747 type) [m].
fields.label: Upper-deck hump height

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip at which the crown starts to rise into the hump (the windshield line of a 747).
fields.label: Hump start station

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip at which the hump reaches its full height; the fore fairing runs from the hump start to here.
fields.label: Hump crown start station

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip at which the aft fairing of the hump starts to descend.
fields.label: Hump crown end station

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip at which the aft fairing of the hump is back on the main crown.
fields.label: Hump end station

fields.help: Exponent of both hump fairings (dimensionless): 2 is tangent to the hump crown, larger gives a fuller hump, 1 a straight ramp. Unset takes 2. Valid 1-4.
fields.label: Hump fairing exponent

fields.help: Height of the upper-deck floor above the main-deck floor under the hump [m].
fields.label: Upper-deck floor height

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip of the forward end of the usable upper-deck floor (aft of the flight deck). Unset takes the hump crown start.
fields.label: Upper-deck start station

fields.help: Distance from the nose tip of the aft end of the usable upper-deck floor. Unset takes the hump crown end.
fields.label: Upper-deck end station

fields.help: Additional validated fuselage sections supplied by the user; edited by the custom-geometry editor rather than the generated scalar form.
Per-station overrides of the generated fuselage loft.
Drawn cabin cross-section: floor and hold polygon.
Embedded lofted outer surface (id under data/lofts); unset keeps the parametric laws.
Number of longitudinal stations used to loft the fuselage body. Higher = smoother surface, slower to draw.
fields.label: Fuselage cross-section count

fields.help: Name from the built-in engine database (see the Engine selector on the Aircraft page): drives thrust, mass, and the default nacelle profile.
fields.label: Engine model

fields.help: Pairs of x-station [m] and radius fraction [0-1 of radius_scale_m] tracing the nacelle silhouette from inlet (x=0) to exit.
fields.label: Nacelle profile points

fields.help: Physical radius the nacelle_profile's fraction-of-1.0 points are scaled by.
fields.label: Nacelle max radius

fields.help: Y-coordinate of each engine's mount position (negative = left/port side); one entry per engine.
fields.label: Engine spanwise (Y) positions

fields.help: Vertical placement of the engine centerline relative to the wing reference plane (negative = below the wing).
fields.label: Engine vertical offset

fields.help: How far forward of the (swept) wing leading edge the nacelle inlet face sits.
fields.label: Inlet offset ahead of wing LE

fields.help: Ratio of bypass (fan duct) to core mass flow. Feeds the mission turbofan network and the Propulsion Analysis on-design cycle.
fields.label: Bypass ratio (BPR)

fields.help: Total pressure ratio through the core compressors (LPC x HPC, not including the fan).
fields.label: Overall (core) pressure ratio (OPR)

fields.help: Pressure ratio across the fan (bypass stream), separate from the core OPR above.
fields.label: Fan pressure ratio (FPR)

fields.help: Combustor-exit stagnation temperature: the primary driver of specific thrust and thermal efficiency in the on-design cycle.
fields.label: Turbine inlet temperature (T4t)

fields.help: Reference cruise thrust-specific fuel consumption for the Breguet payload-range diagram. It is the in-service figure, not the Propulsion Analysis on-design-cycle TSFC.
fields.label: Cruise TSFC (reference)

fields.help: Fan face diameter: informational/reference only (does not currently size the nacelle profile, which comes from radius_scale_m/nacelle_profile above).
fields.label: Fan diameter

fields.help: Fuel flow divided by take-off fuel flow at 7, 30, 85 and 100 % of rated net thrust.
fields.label: Part-power fuel-flow ratios

fields.help: ICAO Engine Emissions Databank UID/variant, or a clearly identified family proxy when an exact entry is unavailable.
fields.label: Part-power schedule source

fields.help: Ratio of wetted (exposed, both sides) surface area to planform area for a thin wing. Used by the drag buildup.
fields.label: Wing wetted-area factor

fields.help: Correction factor on pi*diameter*length for a non-cylindrical (tapered nose/tail) fuselage body.
fields.label: Fuselage wetted-area factor

fields.help: Apply consequence-based transport checks for geometric body angle of attack and usable wing-tank volume.
fields.label: Enable transport-planform constraints

fields.help: Opt in to heuristic penalties on chord ratio, wingbox size, flap footprint, trailing-edge sweep and bending slenderness: airliner-shape preferences. Off by default.
fields.label: Enable transport shape priors

fields.help: Lower bound for the uncorrected geometric body angle of attack after force and moment trim at the nominated cruise point [deg].
fields.label: Geometric body-AoA window: minimum

fields.help: Upper bound for the uncorrected geometric body angle of attack after force and moment trim at the nominated cruise point [deg].
fields.label: Geometric body-AoA window: maximum

fields.help: Minimum available structural depth in the root spar box [m], from local airfoil thickness between the configured spars.
fields.label: Minimum root wingbox depth

fields.help: Minimum available structural depth at the kink station [m], from local airfoil thickness between the spars.
fields.label: Minimum kink wingbox depth

fields.help: Minimum front-to-rear spar separation at the kink station [m].
fields.label: Minimum kink wingbox width

fields.help: Minimum physical trailing-edge flap area divided by wing planform area (dimensionless), from the flap chord and span run.
fields.label: Minimum flap-area fraction

fields.help: Upper bound on projected-span squared over root wingbox width times depth (dimensionless): a preliminary bending-capacity proxy, not wingbox sizing.
fields.label: Maximum root bending-box slenderness

fields.help: Inboard boundary of the wingbox interval credited as fuel volume, as a fraction of semispan.
fields.label: Tankable span start

fields.help: Outboard boundary of the wingbox interval credited as fuel volume, as a fraction of semispan.
fields.label: Tankable span end

fields.help: Upper bound on break_chord_m / root_chord_m (dimensionless); real transports run about 0.45-0.65.
fields.label: Max break/root chord ratio

fields.help: Lower bound on break_chord_m / root_chord_m (dimensionless).
fields.label: Min break/root chord ratio

fields.help: Lower bound on tip_chord_m / root_chord_m (dimensionless).
fields.label: Min tip/root chord ratio

fields.help: Lowest admissible exposed side-of-body-to-kink trailing-edge sweep [deg].
fields.label: Minimum inboard trailing-edge sweep

fields.help: Largest admissible root-to-kink trailing-edge sweep [deg].
fields.label: Maximum inboard trailing-edge sweep

fields.help: Cost returned for any candidate design that raises an exception or fails a hard guard during evaluation.
fields.label: Invalid-design cost

fields.help: The search that runs: mission-sized differential evolution (L-SHADE, epsilon constraints), seeded by a screening sample, with bounded feasibility restoration.
fields.label: Optimization profile

exemption.reason: Retired: the SQP driver was removed; kept so older saved configurations still load.

fields.help: Unused: the SQP driver this setting configured has been removed. Retained so a configuration saved by an earlier build still loads with its value intact.
fields.label: Finite-difference step (retired)

exemption.reason: Retired: the SQP driver was removed; kept so older saved configurations still load.

fields.help: Unused: the SQP driver this setting configured has been removed. Retained so a configuration saved by an earlier build still loads with its value intact.
fields.label: Constraint tolerance (retired)

fields.help: Maximum analysed candidates in this stage; pre-gate rejections do not count. Time-limited refinement may plan a smaller budget.
fields.label: Evaluation ceiling

fields.help: Elapsed-time limit [s], at most 300 s; checked between generations, so a running generation finishes. Ignored when stopping on evaluations only.
fields.label: Time limit [s]

fields.help: Blank for a normal run.
fields.label: Replay evaluation count

fields.help: Refinement only. Blank for a normal run.
fields.label: Replay planned budget

fields.help: Refinement only. Blank for a normal run or one without feasibility restoration.
fields.label: Replay restoration count

fields.help: Largest number of candidates the design-vector pre-gate may reject in this stage before it stops. Blank is 20 times the evaluation budget.
fields.label: Pre-gate rejection cap

fields.help: Maximum analysed candidates in this stage; pre-gate rejections do not count. Time-limited refinement may plan a smaller budget.
fields.label: Evaluation ceiling

fields.help: Elapsed-time limit [s], at most 300 s; checked between generations, so a running generation finishes. Ignored when stopping on evaluations only.
fields.label: Time limit [s]

fields.help: Blank for a normal run.
fields.label: Replay evaluation count

fields.help: Refinement only. Blank for a normal run.
fields.label: Replay planned budget

fields.help: Refinement only. Blank for a normal run or one without feasibility restoration.
fields.label: Replay restoration count

fields.help: Largest number of candidates the design-vector pre-gate may reject in this stage before it stops. Blank is 20 times the evaluation budget.
fields.label: Pre-gate rejection cap

fields.help: Off: static F = 0.5 and CR = 0.9, better than adaptation below 800 evaluations per variable (Tanabe and Fukunaga 2020).
fields.label: Adapt mutation and crossover (L-SHADE)

fields.help: Normalized design-space spread (mean population range over bound width) below which a refinement that has stopped improving is reported as converged rather than stagnated.
fields.label: Convergence spread tolerance

fields.help: Refinement generations with best feasible objective improving by less than 1e-4 (relative) before the search stops as converged or stagnated.
fields.label: Stagnation window

fields.help: Set an integer for a reproducible run (same seed -> same result); leave blank for a different search each run.
fields.label: Random seed

fields.help: Threads a generation's candidates are spread across; 0 uses every thread the machine reports.
fields.label: Native compute worker threads

fields.help: Off: each stage also stops at its time limit (result depends on machine speed).
fields.label: Stop on evaluation budgets only

fields.help: Used by the mission-sized differential_evolution profile. That profile sizes each candidate by the design mission and ranks it feasibility first.
fields.label: Objective

fields.help: Still-air distance from takeoff to the intended destination flown by the design mission with the design payload [nmi].
fields.label: Design range

fields.help: How takeoff mass is set: fixed requirement, mission-iterated up to it or seeded by it, MTOW band around the target, or payload-adjusted with no ceiling.
fields.label: Takeoff mass sizing

fields.help: Centre of the MTOW band [kg]: the search starts at this takeoff mass and the band extends by the band fraction either side. Zero uses the requirement MTOW.
fields.label: MTOW target

fields.help: Half-width of the MTOW band as a fraction of the target: the search may pick any takeoff mass from target x (1 - f) to target x (1 + f).
fields.label: MTOW band fraction

fields.help: Maximum fixed-point passes of empty mass, fuel and takeoff mass before a candidate is reported as not closed. Transport closures normally settle in under ten passes.
fields.label: Sizing iteration limit

fields.help: Change in takeoff mass between two passes below which the sizing loop is taken as closed.
fields.label: Sizing tolerance

fields.help: When takeoff mass is mission-sized, re-trim and re-evaluate the drag polar whenever the CG has moved more than this fraction of MAC since the last trim.
fields.label: Re-trim CG tolerance

fields.help: ICAO Annex 14 aerodrome code letter capping clean-sheet wingspan below the band edge (A 15 m, B 24 m, C 36 m, D 52 m, E 65 m, F 80 m). Auto picks it from the brief.
fields.label: Aerodrome reference code

fields.help: Upper bound on reference approach speed at maximum landing mass for the selected operating or aerodrome category [kt].
fields.label: Maximum approach speed

fields.help: Dimensionless w in the ranking cost J = Q/Qref + w*P, where P sums normalized preference violations; an infeasible candidate adds 1 + H.
fields.label: Preference weight

fields.help: Clean sheet moves every geometry variable inside its global bounds, sizes the fuselage from the cabin and scales the engine rating.
fields.label: Design mode

fields.help: In clean-sheet mode, set the fuselage length to the shortest one whose cabin seats the brief, instead of searching it with an integer seat-count step.
fields.label: Size fuselage from cabin

fields.help: In clean-sheet mode, scale the catalogue engine to the smallest rating meeting every thrust requirement of the closed design.
fields.label: Size engine from requirements

fields.help: Largest departure of the sized engine rating from the catalogue engine's, as a fraction of that rating, up to 0.6.
fields.label: Engine rating window

fields.help: Comma-separated design-variable names that reference adaptation holds at the registered aircraft's values.
fields.label: Fixed variables (reference mode)

fields.help: Half-width of the search window around the reference value for spans, chords, fuselage length and scale factors, as a fraction of it. 0.10 moves a 34 m span 30.6-37.4 m.
fields.label: Reference window, lengths and scales

fields.help: Half-width of the search window around the reference sweep and tip twist.
fields.label: Reference window, angles

fields.help: Half-width of the search window around the reference wing and tail longitudinal positions.
fields.label: Reference window, shifts

fields.help: Half-width of the search window around the reference Hicks-Henne bump amplitudes.
fields.label: Reference window, airfoil bumps

fields.help: Class of a clean-sheet brief: its design-variable guardrails. A registered aircraft keeps the class its preset declares.
fields.label: Aircraft class

fields.help: On by default.
fields.label: Enforce the validity domain

fields.help: Smallest b^2/S accepted (dimensionless), on projected reference span and area. Below this the lifting-line and wingbox correlations extrapolate.
fields.label: Minimum wing aspect ratio

fields.help: Largest b^2/S accepted (dimensionless).
fields.label: Maximum wing aspect ratio

fields.help: Smallest overall length divided by the largest equivalent cross-section diameter (dimensionless).
fields.label: Minimum fuselage fineness ratio

fields.help: Largest length over equivalent diameter (dimensionless). Transport fuselages sit near 8-12; the longest stretches reach about 14.
fields.label: Maximum fuselage fineness ratio

fields.help: Smallest wing quarter-chord to horizontal-tail quarter-chord distance divided by fuselage length (dimensionless, positive aft).
fields.label: Minimum horizontal-tail arm fraction

fields.help: Largest tail arm as a fraction of fuselage length (dimensionless).
fields.label: Maximum horizontal-tail arm fraction

fields.help: Smallest tip chord divided by root chord (dimensionless).
fields.label: Minimum tip-to-root chord ratio

fields.help: Largest tip chord divided by root chord (dimensionless).
fields.label: Maximum tip-to-root chord ratio

fields.help: On by default.
fields.label: Require an ordered trailing-edge break

fields.help: Smallest maximum section thickness at the wing root as a fraction of root chord, dimensionless. Below this the section carries no spar box the structural model can size.
fields.label: Minimum root thickness-to-chord ratio

fields.help: Largest root thickness as a fraction of root chord (dimensionless).
fields.label: Maximum root thickness-to-chord ratio

fields.help: Most negative built geometric washout accepted [deg]: built tip incidence minus root incidence (negative is washout). Registered aircraft run -4 to -7 deg.
fields.label: Most negative built washout

fields.help: Least negative built washout accepted [deg], applied to the root-to-tip difference and every spanwise run.
fields.label: Least negative built washout

fields.help: Wall-clock deadline for final AVL sweeps; independent of the optimizer candidate budget and aerodynamic mesh.
fields.label: AVL reporting timeout

fields.help: Lowest angle of attack evaluated in the final high-fidelity polar sweep.
fields.label: Polar sweep: alpha minimum

fields.help: Highest angle of attack evaluated in the final high-fidelity polar sweep.
fields.label: Polar sweep: alpha maximum

fields.help: How many angle-of-attack points to evaluate between the min/max alpha. More points = smoother drag polar, slower analysis. Part of the Fidelity preset.
fields.label: Polar sweep: number of points

fields.help: Multiplier on each surface's built-in spanwise vortex-lattice panel count. Leave at 1; values above 2 are rejected. Part of the Fidelity preset.
fields.label: VLM spanwise panel resolution

fields.help: Chordwise vortex-lattice panels per strip for the fast in-loop estimate (a count, not a multiplier). 1 reduces the section to a flat plate; 8 is converged.
fields.label: VLM chordwise panel resolution

fields.help: Spanwise panel resolution for the once-per-run final analysis only (polar, trimmed cruise, neutral point). Leave at 1: the span is already converged.
fields.label: Fine VLM spanwise resolution (final analysis)

fields.help: Chordwise panels for the once-per-run final analysis. A supercritical section needs about 8 to resolve its camber; convergence is first order, so 16 is better.
fields.label: Fine VLM chordwise resolution (final analysis)

fields.help: Lower of a two-point alpha pair used for a fast in-loop lift-slope/stability estimate (not the full sweep).
fields.label: Fast-probe alpha (low)

fields.help: Higher of the two-point fast-probe alpha pair.
fields.label: Fast-probe alpha (high)

fields.help: Small horizontal-stabilizer incidence perturbation [deg] used to estimate dCL/di_h and dCm/di_h for the closed-form trim solve. 0.5-2 deg is typical.
fields.label: Trim-solve h-stab incidence probe delta

fields.help: Airspeed used for the autobalance neutral-point probe (finds the CG that gives the target static margin).
fields.label: Autobalance probe airspeed

fields.help: Lower alpha of the two-point pair used to estimate the Cm-Cl slope during autobalance.
fields.label: Autobalance probe alpha (low)

fields.help: Higher alpha of the two-point pair used to estimate the Cm-Cl slope during autobalance.
fields.label: Autobalance probe alpha (high)

fields.help: Ratio of the tail's dynamic pressure to the free stream's (dimensionless); tail lift and moment scale with it. Unset: empirical 0.78 (NASA CR-2144, TN D-3797).
fields.label: Tail dynamic-pressure efficiency (eta_t)

fields.help: Whether to include the geometry-driven fuselage (Munk/Multhopp) destabilising contribution, which moves the neutral point forward.
fields.label: Include fuselage destabilising effect

fields.help: Solve trim and the polar on the Goethert/Prandtl-Glauert stretched lattice at the cruise Mach.
fields.label: Compressible trim (Goethert stretch)

fields.help: Lower CL bound of the window used to fit the parabolic drag polar (CD = CD0 + k*CL^2). Points outside the window are excluded so stall/pre-stall regions don't bias the fit.
fields.label: Drag-polar fit window: CL minimum

fields.help: Upper CL bound of the primary drag-polar fit window.
fields.label: Drag-polar fit window: CL maximum

fields.help: Wider fallback lower CL bound used when the primary fit window captures fewer than 3 points.
fields.label: Drag-polar fit fallback window: CL minimum

fields.help: Wider fallback upper CL bound used when the primary fit window captures fewer than 3 points.
fields.label: Drag-polar fit fallback window: CL maximum

fields.help: Subtract the tapered centre section inside the local fuselage width at the root quarter chord from the parasite wetted area (NASA NDARC exposed-area convention).
fields.label: Exclude buried main-wing area

fields.help: Chordwise location of maximum airfoil thickness (as a fraction of chord), used in the wing form factor.
fields.label: Max-thickness chordwise location

fields.help: How much the wing-fuselage junction disturbs the local flow, multiplying the wing's parasite drag. 1.0 = no interference.
fields.label: Wing interference factor (Q)

fields.help: How much neighbouring components (wing, tail) disturb the fuselage's flow, multiplying its parasite drag.
fields.label: Fuselage interference factor (Q)

fields.help: Multiplier on the summed component parasite drag for leakage and protuberances a build-up cannot see (dimensionless).
fields.label: Viscous drag margin

fields.help: Adds CD_v = fraction * CD0 * CL^2 to the clean drag polar: lift-dependent profile drag an inviscid induced drag cannot see.
fields.label: Lift-dependent viscous drag fraction

fields.help: How much the engine nacelle and pylon disturb the local flow. Typical value 1.3 for podded under-wing installations (Raymer).
fields.label: Nacelle/pylon interference factor (Q)

fields.help: Below this Mach number, transonic wave drag is assumed zero.
fields.label: Wave-drag onset Mach

fields.help: Leading constant of the Lock/Korn wave-drag rise: CD_wave = coefficient * max(M - M_critical, 0)^4 (dimensionless). Must be positive.
fields.label: Wave-drag rise coefficient

fields.help: Maximum lift coefficient achievable in the take-off flap/slat configuration. Drives take-off field length via the matching chart.
fields.label: Max lift coefficient, take-off (CLmax_TO)

exemption.reason: Provenance label for CLmax_TO; shown in reports and the fleet-check example, never enters a calculation.

fields.help: Reference for CLmax_TO.
fields.label: Takeoff maximum lift source

fields.help: Maximum lift coefficient achievable in the landing flap/slat configuration. Drives landing distance.
fields.label: Max lift coefficient, landing (CLmax_L)

exemption.reason: Provenance label for CLmax_land; shown in reports and the fleet-check example, never enters a calculation.

fields.help: Reference for CLmax_land, including the published landing mass and approach speed when derived from an aircraft source.
fields.label: Landing maximum lift source

fields.help: Reproduce the translated jet correlation for every propulsion type, with its extra balanced-field multiplier and approach-speed factor.
fields.label: Use legacy field correlations

fields.help: During optimization, scale the declared clean, take-off and landing CLmax with the candidate wing sweep and flap area. Off keeps the declared values.
fields.label: Scale CLmax with wing geometry

fields.help: Raise take-off safety speed V2 above the schedule when needed to meet the CS 25.121(b) second-segment gradient, and charge the longer field. Jets only.
fields.label: Improved-climb take-off speed

fields.help: Resolved improved-climb take-off safety speed over the reference stall speed. Written by the analysis, not a user input.
Judge cruise-altitude thrust requirements with the engine deck's thrust at cruise Mach and altitude instead of a flat lapse ratio. Off restores the flat ratio.
fields.label: Cruise thrust from the engine deck

fields.help: Dry hard-runway rolling coefficient for the propeller takeoff calculation.
Mean dry-runway reject deceleration divided by standard gravity.
Sea-level inertia-distance allowance in the preliminary balanced-field model.
Mean landing airborne drag minus thrust divided by weight.
Mean dry-concrete landing deceleration divided by gravity.
Share of available runway usable by the unfactored dry landing distance.
Maximum lift coefficient in the clean configuration (flaps/slats up): the stall limit of the V-n diagram, distinct from the take-off and landing values.
fields.label: Max lift coefficient, clean (CLmax_clean)

fields.help: Part of the take-off and landing CLmax increments given by the slats or Kruegers: slats out, flaps up, less clean. Geometry scaling moves it with the slat span and the sweep.
fields.label: Leading-edge CLmax increment

fields.help: Most negative (inverted-flight) lift coefficient in clean configuration: the negative stall boundary on the V-n diagram.
fields.label: Min lift coefficient, clean (CLmin_clean)

fields.help: Fraction by which static sea-level thrust falls off during the take-off ground roll / initial climb, used in the matching-chart take-off constraint.
fields.label: Thrust lapse ratio

fields.help: Conceptual fallback gradient for an engine count outside the implemented 14 CFR 25.121(b) table.
fields.label: OEI 2nd-segment climb gradient (fallback)

fields.help: Empirical constant relating approach speed / wing loading to landing ground-roll + air distance.
fields.label: Landing distance factor (k_land)

fields.help: Legacy constant lift coefficient for the conceptual one-engine-inoperative second-segment L/D (Raymer Ch. 17).
fields.label: OEI climb configuration CL

fields.help: Take-off flap/slat drag increment on the reference wing area, gear retracted (14 CFR 25.121(b) configuration).
fields.label: OEI climb high-lift drag increment (gear up)

fields.help: Drag increment of the extended landing gear on the reference wing area in take-off (14 CFR 25.121(a)). Default 0.020 (Roskam Part I, Table 3.6: 0.015-0.025).
fields.label: Landing-gear drag increment, take-off

fields.help: Landing flap/slat drag increment on the reference wing area, gear retracted (14 CFR 25.121(d) approach climb).
fields.label: Landing flap/slat drag increment

fields.help: Drag increment of the extended landing gear on the reference wing area in landing (approach, flare, 14 CFR 25.119).
fields.label: Landing-gear drag increment, landing

fields.help: Ratio of thrust available 8 s after advancing from flight idle (CS 25.119) to full go-around thrust. 1.0 is the non-conservative bound; about 0.95 is defensible.
fields.label: Go-around thrust fraction at 8 s (spool-up)

fields.help: CS 25.107(b): minimum take-off safety speed as a multiple of stall speed VSR: 1.13 for most turbojets and twin/tri turboprops, 1.08 for four-engine turboprops.
fields.label: V2MIN / VSR

fields.help: Declared wheels per main-gear truck; selects the jet landing braking deceleration (Torenbeek): 0.40 g for two wheels, 0.32 g for four. 0 is treated as four.
fields.label: Main-gear wheels per truck (0 = undeclared)

fields.help: Apply the wet-runway landing distance factor: EU CAT.POL.A.235(a)(2) requires 115 % of the dry distance when no wet data exist. Off by default.
fields.label: Wet landing runway

fields.help: Half-width of the accepted band for closed take-off mass over the take-off mass the engine was designed for.
fields.label: Engine-to-mass match tolerance

fields.help: Optional manual override of the installed thrust ratio (condition to SLS) for CS 25.121 engine-out checks. Empty takes it from the engine deck at V2.
fields.label: OEI thrust at V2 / rated SLS thrust

fields.help: Optional manual override of the asymmetric trim drag coefficient at V2 (reference wing area).
fields.label: OEI asymmetric trim/control drag increment

fields.help: Optional manual override of the failed-engine drag coefficient at V2 (reference wing area).
fields.label: OEI inoperative-engine/windmilling drag increment

fields.help: Trailing-edge flap deflection of the take-off setting, from the aircraft's documents. Empty: the default of 20 deg applies.
fields.label: Take-off flap deflection

fields.help: Largest certified landing flap deflection, from the aircraft's documents. Empty: the default of 35 deg applies.
fields.label: Landing flap deflection

fields.help: Lower wing-loading (W/S) axis limit on the matching chart plot. Widen for very light (GA) aircraft. (~204 kg/m^2)
fields.label: Matching chart wing-loading axis: minimum

fields.help: Upper wing-loading (W/S) axis limit on the matching chart plot. Widen for very heavy (freighter) aircraft. (~1020 kg/m^2)
fields.label: Matching chart wing-loading axis: maximum

fields.help: Additional historical multiplier used only by the legacy field path; the corrected jet TOP correlation ignores it.
fields.label: Balanced field length factor

fields.help: Declared minimum-control speed as a multiple of take-off reference stall speed VSR.
fields.label: VMC / VS_TO

fields.help: FAR 25.107: rotation speed must be at least 1.05*VMC.
fields.label: VR / VMC floor

fields.help: FAR 25.107: rotation speed must also be at least 1.10*VS_TO. VR = max(vr_vmc_factor*VMC, vr_vstall_factor*VS_TO).
fields.label: VR / VS_TO floor

fields.help: Selected take-off safety speed as a multiple of reference stall speed VSR.
fields.label: V2 / VS_TO

fields.help: Decision speed V1 as a fraction of rotation speed VR. On a dry balanced field V1 sits just below VR (about 0.95-0.98).
fields.label: V1 / VR

fields.help: Approach-speed multiple retained for translated legacy results. The corrected method uses Vref = 1.23 VS1g, approximating the non-icing 14 CFR 25.125 VSR0 floor.
fields.label: VAPP / VS_land

fields.help: Touchdown speed as a multiple of landing stall speed.
fields.label: VTD / VS_land

fields.help: Number of wing-loading points swept when drawing the matching-chart constraint curves. A plotting resolution only: higher is smoother but slower.
fields.label: Matching chart plot resolution

fields.help: The method that owns every mass group.
fields.label: Mass architecture

fields.help: FLOPS VMAX: the maximum operating or design Mach number. Cruise Mach is not substituted because the two are different certification quantities.
fields.label: Maximum Mach number

fields.help: FLOPS DESRNG from a revision-locked aircraft design source. A marketing maximum or the selected airport route is not silently substituted.
fields.label: Design range

fields.help: Installed flight-deck crew used by the FLOPS instruments, electrical, avionics, furnishings, and operating-item equations.
fields.label: Flight crew count

fields.help: Installed cabin flight attendants. Follows the cabin layout: never fewer than one per 50 passenger seats (EASA ORO.CC.100, 14 CFR 121.391); a larger value you enter is kept.
fields.label: Flight attendant count

fields.help: Installed galley-service crew. Enter zero explicitly when the aircraft carries none.
fields.label: Galley crew count

fields.help: Off (Auto): the class counts and the cabin crew follow the cabin layout and one attendant per 50 seats. On: the values below are used as entered.
fields.label: Manual cabin and crew inputs

fields.help: Follows the cabin layout automatically: the installed first-class seat count comes from the Cabin class configuration; edit the cabin to change it.
fields.label: First-class passenger count

fields.help: Follows the cabin layout automatically: the installed business-class seat count comes from the Cabin class configuration; edit the cabin to change it.
fields.label: Business-class passenger count

fields.help: Follows the cabin layout automatically: the installed economy/tourist seat count comes from the Cabin class configuration; edit the cabin to change it.
fields.label: Tourist-class passenger count

fields.help: Declared hydraulic working pressure. The FLOPS 3,000 psi reference appears inside its equation; it is not a missing-input default.
fields.label: Hydraulic system pressure

fields.help: FLOPS VARSWP: enter 0 for a declared fixed wing and 1 for full variable sweep. Absence is not treated as fixed geometry.
fields.label: Variable-sweep penalty

fields.help: FLOPS FNEW. This is declared because a centerline engine cannot be classified safely from coordinates alone.
fields.label: Wing-mounted engine count

fields.help: FLOPS FNEF, including empennage-mounted installations. Wing and fuselage counts must sum to the built engine count.
fields.label: Fuselage-mounted engine count

fields.help: FLOPS NTANK: physical tanks represented by the declared fuel-system topology.
fields.label: Fuel tank count

fields.help: FLOPS FMXTOT: source-backed maximum usable fuel capacity across wing, fuselage, and auxiliary tanks.
fields.label: Maximum usable fuel capacity

fields.help: Whether the aircraft carries an APU. NASA FLOPS equation 101 is evaluated when true; an architecture with hotel power from an installed engine declares false.
fields.label: Auxiliary power unit installed

fields.help: Cargo loaded into standardized containers for FLOPS WCON. Enter zero explicitly when no containerized cargo is carried.
fields.label: Containerized cargo mass

fields.help: Whether the holds are loose-loaded (bulk), containerized (ULD) or mixed. FLOPS eqs. 125-126 charge 175 lb of container per 950 lb of containerized mass.
fields.label: Cargo hold loading

fields.help: Read only for mixed hold loading: the fraction of checked baggage in unit load devices rather than loose bulk (0-1), normally the containerized share of hold volume.
fields.label: Containerized baggage fraction

fields.help: FLOPS eq. 110 and operating-item eqs. 119-126 as published, or the LTH civil-transport relations.
fields.label: Cabin equipment method

fields.help: Read only by the LTH cabin-equipment method, which has separate operating-item relations for short/medium-haul and long-haul aircraft.
fields.label: Operating haul class

fields.help: Mission, cabin, and installed-architecture provenance required before FLOPS can report a verified component buildup.
FLOPS wing bending material factor: the simplified trapezoidal fit (eq. 10) or the detailed load-path integration (eqs. 18-32) over the built planform.
fields.label: Wing bending-factor method

fields.help: FLOPS FCOMP, composite utilization factor for wing structure: 0 for no composites to 1 for maximum use (NASA/TM-2017-219627). Not a material percentage.
fields.label: Wing composite utilization

fields.help: FLOPS FAERT: 0 for no aeroelastic tailoring, 1 for the maximum tailoring benefit in the wing bending material.
fields.label: Aeroelastic tailoring factor

fields.help: FLOPS FSTRT: 0 for a cantilever wing, 1 for full benefit from strut bracing.
fields.label: Wing strut-bracing factor

fields.help: FLOPS PCTL: fraction of the aircraft load carried by the defined wing. 1 for a conventional single wing.
fields.label: Wing load fraction

fields.help: FLOPS CARGF: 0 for a passenger transport fuselage, 1 for a military cargo transport floor (38 percent fuselage structure penalty).
fields.label: Military cargo floor factor

fields.help: FLOPS DG, design gross mass [kg] for the wing, tail, fuselage, control and pod-relief equations. Blank uses the takeoff mass being evaluated.
fields.label: Structural design gross mass

fields.help: FLOPS WLDG for the landing-gear equations. Blank uses the maximum landing mass fraction of the mass model applied to the design gross mass.
fields.label: Design landing mass

fields.help: FLOPS XMLG, length of the extended main-gear oleo [m].
fields.label: Main-gear oleo length

fields.help: FLOPS XNLG: length of the extended nose landing-gear oleo. Blank uses 70 percent of the main-gear length (equation 67).
fields.label: Nose-gear oleo length

fields.help: Certified maximum operating altitude [m]. Sizes the pressurized shell of the regional turboprop class for the differential against an 8,000 ft cabin.
fields.label: Maximum operating altitude

fields.help: Maximum zero-fuel mass [kg] for the fuselage bending term of the regional turboprop pressurized fuselage method. Blank uses the structural design gross mass.
fields.label: Design zero-fuel mass

fields.help: FLOPS WPAINT, paint mass per wetted area [kg/m^2] on wings, tails, fuselage and nacelles. Validated NASA decks use 0.1807 kg/m^2 (0.037 lbm/ft^2); zero means unpainted.
fields.label: Paint area density

fields.help: Published FLOPS has no pylon term.
fields.label: Pylon mass method

fields.help: FLOPS WENGB, declared dry mass of the baseline engine [kg]. Blank uses the FLOPS estimate of baseline thrust over 5.5 (eq. 76).
fields.label: Baseline engine mass

fields.help: FLOPS THRSO: sea-level static rated thrust of the baseline engine the mass is scaled from. Blank uses the installed engine's rated thrust, so the scaling ratio is one.
fields.label: Baseline engine thrust

fields.help: FLOPS EEXP, exponent on the thrust ratio when the baseline engine is scaled (eq. 75). Values below 0.3 give a linear mass-per-thrust slope. Default 1.15.
fields.label: Engine mass scaling exponent

fields.help: Whether the declared engine dry mass already includes the starter system.
fields.label: Engine starter scope

fields.help: FLOPS WINLB, inlet mass of the baseline engine [kg], declared separately (eq. 77). Blank means it is already in the engine mass.
fields.label: Baseline inlet mass

fields.help: FLOPS EINL: exponent on the thrust ratio when the baseline inlet is scaled (equation 77). The FLOPS default is 1.
fields.label: Inlet mass scaling exponent

fields.help: FLOPS WNOZB, nozzle mass of the baseline engine [kg], declared separately (eq. 78). Blank means it is already in the engine mass. Needs an explicit baseline engine mass.
fields.label: Baseline nozzle mass

fields.help: Whether the baseline engine mass includes the nozzle, declares it as a separate eq. 78 term, or leaves it outside or unknown (no nozzle mass is invented).
fields.label: Engine nozzle scope

fields.help: FLOPS ENOZ: exponent on the thrust ratio when the baseline nozzle is scaled (equation 78). The FLOPS default is 1.
fields.label: Nozzle mass scaling exponent

fields.help: Include the FLOPS thrust-reverser mass of 3.4 percent of rated thrust per nacelle (equation 86). Disable for an installation without reversers.
fields.label: Thrust reversers installed

fields.help: The number of engines fitted with a thrust reverser, when only some reverse. Blank charges equation 86 on every nacelle (FLOPS TNAC).
fields.label: Engines with thrust reversers

fields.help: FLOPS WPMISC: declared propulsion-system mass added to the engine controls and starters (equation 91).
fields.label: Miscellaneous propulsion mass

fields.help: FLOPS WMARG expressed as a fraction of the computed structural, propulsion and systems mass, added to the empty mass (equation 139). Zero adds no margin.
fields.label: Empty-mass margin fraction

fields.help: Certificated dry mass of one engine [kg]; for the PW100 family it includes the reduction gearbox.
fields.label: Engine dry mass

fields.help: Take-off shaft power of the engine the declared dry mass was measured at [kW].
fields.label: Baseline engine shaft power

fields.help: Exponent on the shaft-power ratio when scaling a declared engine dry mass to another rating (dimensionless). 1 gives the linear NASA GASP relation.
fields.label: Engine mass scaling exponent

fields.help: The certificated PW100 dry weight already includes the gearbox, so a separate gearbox estimate would be counted twice.
fields.label: Gearbox inside engine mass

fields.help: Number of blades on one propeller, the Hamilton Standard B of NASA CR-152303 Vol. V equation V.1.28.
fields.label: Propeller blade count

fields.help: Hamilton Standard blade activity factor A.F. per blade (NASA CR-152303 Vol. V equation V.1.28). Zero blocks the propeller mass instead of assuming a value.
fields.label: Blade activity factor

fields.help: Blade material and pitch-change hardware.
fields.label: Propeller construction

fields.help: Hamilton Standard K_w (dimensionless). Blank uses the published constant (355 double-acting aluminium, 220 single-acting).
fields.label: Propeller weight coefficient

fields.help: Spinner, blade de-icing and governor mass for one propeller [kg].
fields.label: Propeller accessory mass

fields.help: Optional source-backed mass of one propeller item. When present it replaces the generic Hamilton Standard regression; clear it when changing the propeller design.
fields.label: Propeller assembly mass

fields.help: Scope of a declared propeller assembly mass.
fields.label: Assembly includes accessories

fields.help: NASA GASP UW_NAC (CR-152303 eq. V.1.6): an empirical nacelle component area coefficient, not a material density; a declared model input.
fields.label: Nacelle area density

fields.help: Optional source-backed mass of one nacelle component [kg], used with the reference area below.
fields.label: Nacelle reference component mass

fields.help: Optional reference wetted area of one nacelle matching the reference component mass [m^2].
fields.label: Nacelle reference area

fields.help: NASA GASP F_PYL (CR-152303 eq. V.1.7): W_PYLON = F_PYL (W_ENG + W_NAC)^0.736 for multi-engine installations.
fields.label: Pylon coefficient

fields.help: Engine controls, starters, mounts, fire protection and installation accessories for all engines together [kg].
fields.label: Engine installation mass

fields.help: Engine oil for all installed engines together [kg]. FLOPS eq. 123 uses rated thrust and eq. 162 is unusable as printed, so this is declared.
fields.label: Engine oil mass

fields.help: Place mass groups at built geometry stations (tails at 42 % mean chord, gear, engines at nacelles, fuel in tanks).
fields.label: Geometry-derived component stations

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: fraction of MTOW treated as suspended mass in the Torenbeek wing structural formula [0-1]. Typical commercial transport 0.70-0.78.
fields.label: Wing suspended-mass fraction

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: design airspeed with flaps extended, fed into the Torenbeek wing-mass formula.
fields.label: Max airspeed with flaps extended

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: maximum flap deflection angle, fed into the Torenbeek wing-mass formula.
fields.label: Max take-off flap deflection

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: landing gear mass as a fraction of MTOW. Raymer Table 15.2: ~4% for commercial jet transports.
fields.label: Landing-gear mass fraction

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: dry engine mass is estimated as thrust / (this factor * g). Historical engine thrust-to-weight ratios are ~5-7, so this factor is typically ~6.
fields.label: Engine thrust-to-weight factor

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: multiplier on dry engine mass accounting for pylon, cowling, fire suppression and other installed accessories.
fields.label: Propulsion installation overhead

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: fallback propulsion mass as a fraction of MTOW, used only if the selected engine isn't found in the database.
fields.label: Propulsion mass fallback fraction

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: avionics, electrical, ECS, APU, etc. as a fraction of MTOW. Raymer Table 15.2: 9-13% for commercial transports.
fields.label: Systems & equipment mass fraction

fields.help: Legacy comparison only: passenger seats, galleys, lavatories, insulation, crew, paint, and operational empty items as a fraction of MTOW. Typically 10-14% for passenger transports.
fields.label: Furnishings & operations mass fraction

fields.help: Payload mass per metre of occupied cabin length [kg/m]. Used only to place the payload/systems CG, not the payload mass.
fields.label: Payload linear density

fields.help: Nose landing gear longitudinal position, as a fraction of total fuselage length from the nose.
fields.label: Nose-gear X position

fields.help: Main landing gear longitudinal position, as a fraction of the mean aerodynamic chord aft of the MAC leading edge.
fields.label: Main-gear X position
fields.unit: fraction of MAC aft of MAC LE

fields.help: Maximum fraction of total aircraft weight the nose gear is rated to carry: sets the 'NLG Max Strength' CG-envelope boundary.
fields.label: Max nose-gear load fraction

fields.help: Maximum fraction of total aircraft weight the main gear is rated to carry: sets the 'MLG Max Strength' CG-envelope boundary.
fields.label: Max main-gear load fraction

fields.help: Minimum fraction of weight on the nose gear at the most-aft CG, setting the Min Nose Load CG boundary. Class value 0.0352: the lowest share at a certified most-aft CG in 13 airliner families.
fields.label: Min nose-gear load fraction

fields.help: Maximum fraction of weight on the nose gear at the forward CG limit. Raymer 6th ed. Sec. 11.2: above 0.20 the main gear is too far aft (0.15 preferred); 0.05 is the same pair's aft-CG minimum.
fields.label: Max nose-gear handling-load fraction

fields.help: Maximum Landing Weight (MLW) as a fraction of MTOW, shown as a reference line on the CG envelope.
fields.label: Max landing weight fraction of MTOW

fields.help: Jet-A/Jet-A1 density at 15C (~804 kg/m^3). Converts wing tank volume to a fuel-mass capacity for the payload-range diagram and the wing fuel-volume check.
fields.label: Fuel density

fields.help: Fraction of the wing's geometric (Torenbeek) fuel volume that is usable tank capacity, after structure, ribs, systems and unusable fuel [0-1].
fields.label: Usable fuel-tank volume fraction

fields.help: Margin applied to the static reaction load when selecting tire count (dimensionless), so rated tire load is never fully used by static load alone.
fields.label: Tire load safety factor

fields.help: Wheels on the nose gear strut. 0 = auto: 1 for light aircraft, 2 (the near-universal choice for CS-25/FAR-25 transports) once MTOW exceeds nlg_dual_wheel_mtow_kg.
fields.label: Nose-gear wheel count (0 = auto)

fields.help: Auto-sizing switches from a single to a dual (twin) nose wheel above this MTOW: below it, transport-category aircraft still commonly fly single nose wheels.
fields.label: MTOW threshold for dual nose wheels

fields.help: Number of main-gear legs, left and right combined. 0 is auto: 2 below mlg_body_gear_mtow_kg, 4 (adds centreline body gear, A380/747 class) above it.
fields.label: Main-gear strut count (0 = auto)

fields.help: Auto-sizing adds two centreline body-gear legs (4 main legs total) above this MTOW.
fields.label: MTOW threshold for body (centreline) main gear

fields.help: 0 = auto: the smallest of {2, 4, 6} standard bogie sizes whose rated capacity (tire_safety_factor-derated) covers this strut's static reaction load at the aft CG limit.
fields.label: Wheels per main-gear strut (0 = auto)

fields.help: Main-gear lateral track as a multiple of fuselage diameter (dimensionless).
fields.label: Main-gear track / fuselage-diameter factor

fields.help: Published nose-gear to primary main-gear wheelbase, kept for comparison [m].
fields.label: Reference landing-gear wheelbase

fields.help: Published nose-gear to body-main-gear wheelbase kept for a distinct source comparison [m].
fields.label: Reference body-gear wheelbase

fields.help: Published main-gear track used as a source baseline when its definition matches the layout [m].
fields.label: Reference main-gear track

fields.help: Optional bogie counts per strut in layout order: left wing, right wing, then centreline/body gear. Use even counts (2, 4 or 6), one per main-gear strut.
fields.label: Main-gear wheels by strut

fields.help: Which reference tire class to size with: 'auto' picks the smallest class whose rated load, with at most 6 wheels per strut, covers the static gear loads.
fields.label: Tire class

fields.help: Certified main-gear tire designation as printed in the aircraft documents (for example H49x19.0-22/32PR). 'auto' sizes from the tire class.
fields.label: Main-gear tire

fields.help: Certified nose-gear tire designation as printed in the aircraft documents (for example 49x17/32PR). 'auto' sizes from the tire class.
fields.label: Nose-gear tire

fields.help: Landing-gear strut material, shown on the planform diagram and report. 'auto' selects by MTOW class (300M-class steel for larger transports).
fields.label: Strut material

fields.help: Maximum lateral tip-over angle from vertical at the forward CG limit [deg] (Raymer Ch. 11 / Currey). 63 deg is the transport-category limit.
fields.label: Max lateral turnover angle

fields.help: Deceleration for the nose-gear dynamic braking reaction, in g. 14 CFR 25.733(b)(2): 1.0 g down with 0.31 g forward; load must not exceed 1.5x the static rating.
fields.label: Nose-gear dynamic braking deceleration

fields.help: A tire's dynamic (braking) rated load as a multiple of its static rating (dimensionless). 14 CFR 25.733(b) caps nose-gear braking load at 1.5x.
fields.label: Tire dynamic-rating factor

fields.help: Optional extra floor on the longitudinal tip-back angle at the most-aft main axle and most-aft CG [deg]. It must always clear the tail-scrape angle.
fields.label: Minimum tip-back angle floor

fields.help: Pitch attitude reachable at rotation (VR) without tail scrape [deg]: the tail-scrape angle must be at least this. 10 deg is typical of transports, an assumption.
fields.label: Required rotation angle at lift-off

fields.help: Static strut length (belly clearance) from the fuselage lower surface to the ground line [m].
fields.label: Fuselage-to-ground clearance

fields.help: Optional override of the required pitch angular acceleration at rotation in the forward-CG nose-wheel-liftoff balance [deg/s^2].
fields.label: Rotation pitch angular acceleration

fields.help: Optional override of the pitch radius of gyration r_y, as a fraction of MAC, in the nose-wheel-liftoff balance.
fields.label: Pitch radius of gyration (fraction of MAC)

fields.help: Whether the horizontal stabiliser is trimmable (a THS, as on jet transports), set before takeoff for the takeoff CG.
fields.label: Trimmable stabiliser

fields.help: Nose-up takeoff setting of a trimmable stabiliser against the fuselage reference line [deg].
fields.label: Takeoff stabiliser nose-up setting

fields.help: Largest nose-up setting of the trimmable stabiliser from the flight-control data (FCOM or AMM) [deg].
fields.label: Stabiliser nose-up travel

fields.help: Trailing-edge-up elevator travel at takeoff rotation [deg, positive], used by the forward-CG nose-wheel-liftoff balance.
fields.label: Elevator up travel at rotation

fields.help: Wing-body lift coefficient at the ground attitude at V_R, as a fraction of CLmax_TO [0-1]: before rotation the angle of attack is low and gear-limited.
fields.label: Ground-attitude CL (fraction of CLmax_TO)

fields.help: Tire rolling-friction coefficient on a dry paved runway during the takeoff roll (dimensionless). 0.02 is the usual conceptual value; an estimate.
fields.label: Rolling friction coefficient at rotation

fields.label: Target passenger share [%]

fields.label: Seats abreast
