fields.help: Checked-bag mass carried in the hold per seated passenger [kg]. Part of the combined mass per passenger: changing it moves mass between cabin and hold, not the total.
fields.label: Checked baggage per passenger

fields.help: Carry freight on the main deck, as a dedicated freighter does, rather than only in the lower holds. A passenger aircraft has no main-deck cargo.
Unit load device code for the main deck: the pallets and boxes a freighter's main deck takes, which are far larger than anything that fits a lower hold.
Loading format for lower holds, including passenger baggage.
How to place the load: 'target_cg' trims to the target CG, 'min_pallets' concentrates full containers, 'door_proximity' favours doors, 'uniform' spreads evenly.
Centre of gravity the load is trimmed toward [% MAC].
Longitudinal position of the main-deck cargo door. 0 places it at mid-cabin, which is what the door-proximity strategy measures distance from.
Longitudinal position of the forward lower-hold door. 0 places it against the forward hold.
Longitudinal position of the aft lower-hold door. 0 places it against the aft hold.
How much payload the centre-of-gravity trim moves between positions per iteration. A smaller step trims more precisely and needs more iterations to get there.
Iteration cap for the CG trim. A very large aircraft with small steps may need more than the default; raise this rather than the step if the trim does not converge.
How checked baggage is split between hold compartments: 'target_cg' trims toward the balance target, 'volume_proportional' splits by compartment volume.
Declared baggage compartments with station extent, volume and optional net-mass limit. Empty means the compartments are derived from the fuselage geometry.
Declared freight hold (floor, ramp, clear width and height) of a military transport or freighter.
Stowage density of freight and baggage [kg/m^3]: a container carries at most its volume times this.
Clear height of the main-deck cargo door [m]: a freighter's pallets are built up to the fuselage section, but no higher than this opening passes. Unset builds them up to the section.
Declared zones and point masses.
Fly the design along the configured route in a normal Run, producing block fuel and trajectory figures.
Not used: the mission analysis is not stopped by a time limit. Kept so existing configuration files still load.
Directory holding the navigation data the airway router reads. Downloaded on demand rather than distributed with the program.
Image the route globe is drawn on. Downloaded on demand rather than distributed with the program.
Directory holding saved and imported route files.
Number of points a great-circle route is sampled at when no airway or dispatched routing is available. Higher is smoother on the globe and costs nothing else.
Reject generated airway detours above this ratio to great-circle distance (dimensionless) and use the great circle instead.
fields.label: Maximum airway route stretch

fields.help: Read complete endpoints from coordinate-bearing airway data, including navaids absent from the fix catalog. Turn off with maximum airway stretch 0 to reproduce legacy routing.
fields.label: Use airway endpoint coordinates

fields.help: Dispatch account name or pilot ID. When set, routing tries this account's latest flight plan before imported or great-circle routing. Blank skips it.
Time limit for fetching a filed flight plan before falling through to the other routing tiers. Set on Workspace > External Tools.
If your latest SimBrief OFP is for a different city pair than the airports selected above, fly the OFP's pair instead (the most accurate route available).
fields.label: SimBrief overrides route airports

fields.help: Whether the takeoff, climb, descent and landing airspeeds are true airspeeds (legacy default) or calibrated airspeeds resolved at each leg's altitude.
Mach held on the climb legs above the altitude where the calibrated airspeed schedule reaches it (the CAS/Mach crossover). Zero: constant calibrated airspeed all the way up.
Mach held on the descent legs above the CAS/Mach crossover altitude, with the calibrated airspeed schedule below it. Zero: constant calibrated airspeed from the top of descent.
Maximum operating Mach number (MMO) from the type certificate data sheet. No climb or descent leg is flown above it and the cruise legs are held to it. Zero: not declared.
Maximum operating calibrated airspeed (VMO) from the type certificate data sheet [m/s]; no leg flies faster. Zero is undeclared (jet cruise is then held to VD / 1.25).

VMO from the type certificate data sheet where it varies with altitude: pairs of pressure altitude [m] and VMO [m/s calibrated], straight lines between rows, a step as two rows at one altitude. Replaces the single VMO when set.
fields.label: VMO by pressure altitude

fields.help: MMO from the type certificate data sheet where it varies with altitude: pairs of pressure altitude [m] and MMO, straight lines between rows, a step as two rows at one altitude. Replaces the single MMO when set.
fields.label: MMO by pressure altitude

fields.help: Maximum flap-extended speed (VFE) of the landing flap from the type certificate data sheet [m/s calibrated]. The approach rung (descent 4) and the landing are flown at or below it, so the aircraft has slowed below VFE before the landing configuration is extended. Zero: not declared.
Time from brake release to lift-off flown at take-off rating [s], added to the trip as a labelled fuel and time allowance.
Cruise level rule: declared altitude, design altitude, or optimum initial level (300 ft/min residual climb at top of climb) with step climbs.
Height above the departure field the takeoff segment climbs to before the initial climb takes over.
Airspeed flown from liftoff to the end of the takeoff segment.
Rate of climb flown during the takeoff segment.
Airspeed flown from the end of the takeoff segment to the first cruise step.
Rate of climb flown up to the first cruise step. The steepest of the three climb segments, since the aircraft is at its lightest thrust-to-weight advantage low down.
Altitude the initial climb levels off at, as a fraction of the cruise altitude, so raising the cruise level moves this step up with it.
Airspeed flown during the first step climb.
Rate of climb during the first step climb. Much shallower than the initial climb: the aircraft is heavy, high, and trading only a little altitude for cruise efficiency.
Altitude the first step climb levels off at, as a fraction of the cruise altitude.
Airspeed flown during the second step climb, which reaches the final cruise altitude.
Rate of climb during the second step climb, the shallowest of the profile.
Airspeed flown on the first cruise leg.
Relative share of the distance remaining after climb and descent legs flown on the first cruise leg. Active cruise fractions are normalized so the route closes exactly.
Airspeed flown on the second cruise leg, slower than the first as the aircraft climbs and lightens.
Relative share of the distance remaining after profile climb and descent legs flown on the second cruise leg.
Airspeed flown on the third and final cruise leg.
Relative share of the distance remaining after climb and descent legs flown on the third cruise leg. Active cruise fractions are normalized so the route closes exactly.
Altitude the first descent rung levels off at. A rung below the arrival field's elevation is skipped rather than flown.
Airspeed flown down to the first descent rung's altitude.
Rate of descent flown down to the first rung's altitude.
Altitude the second descent rung levels off at.
Airspeed flown down to the second descent rung's altitude.
Rate of descent flown down to the second rung's altitude.
Altitude the third descent rung levels off at, the usual speed-limit altitude below which airspeed is restricted.
Airspeed flown down to the third descent rung's altitude.
Rate of descent flown down to the third rung's altitude.
Altitude the fourth descent rung levels off at, where the approach begins.
Airspeed flown down to the fourth descent rung's altitude.
Rate of descent flown down to the fourth rung's altitude.
Airspeed flown on the final descent to the arrival field's elevation: an approach speed, well below the descent rungs above it.
Rate of descent flown on the final descent to the arrival field's elevation.
The mission as a list of stages (take-off, climbs, cruises, holds, descents, diversions, landing) with payload and fuel events. Empty flies the standard mission.
Still-air distance of the route this run planned [m].
Run an MSES 2-D polar sweep on the optimized root airfoil in a normal Run, filling the Model Comparison tab. On by default.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.help: Folder containing mset.exe, mses.exe and mplot.exe (absolute or repo-relative). MSES is licensed separately by MIT and is not distributed with ALAS.
fields.label: MSES executables directory

fields.help: Optional path to the double-precision osmapDP.dat used by MSES free-transition calculations.
fields.label: MSES Orr-Sommerfeld database

fields.help: Max time allowed for one mesh-generation (mset) call before it's killed.
fields.label: MSET timeout

fields.help: Max time allowed for one flow-solve (mses) call before it's killed.
fields.label: MSES timeout

fields.help: Newton iteration cap per angle of attack: MSES reports non-convergence rather than looping forever, but a hard cap keeps a single stubborn point from stalling the whole sweep.
fields.label: Max solver iterations

fields.help: e^N transition critical amplification factor (dimensionless). 9 is the standard clean-flight default (Drela); 4-5 gives earlier transition in rough environments.
fields.label: Transition N-crit

fields.help: Force transition at this upper-surface x/c instead of letting MSES predict it. 1.0 = free (natural) transition, the realistic default for a clean cruise wing.
fields.label: Forced transition x/c, upper surface

fields.help: Force transition at this lower-surface x/c. 1.0 = free (natural) transition.
fields.label: Forced transition x/c, lower surface

fields.help: The MSES polar sweeps [trim_alpha - this, trim_alpha + this] so the comparison brackets the actual cruise operating point, not an arbitrary fixed range.
fields.label: Alpha sweep half-width around the trimmed design point

fields.help: Number of angle-of-attack points in the MSES polar sweep.
fields.label: Alpha sweep point count

fields.help: Number of surface panel nodes MSET generates for the airfoil mesh.
fields.label: MSET panel count (n)

fields.help: Streamwise grid stretching parameter for the MSET mesh: larger values cluster more points near the airfoil.
fields.label: MSET grid density exponent (e)

fields.help: MSES artificial-dissipation coefficient. 1.0 is its normal second-order setting; a negative value disables second-order dissipation and is reserved for legacy parity replay.
Leading-edge slat chord as a fraction of local wing chord.
fields.label: Slat chord fraction

fields.help: Inboard end of the slat run, as a fraction of wing semi-span from the root.
fields.label: Slat span start

fields.help: Outboard end of the slat run, as a fraction of wing semi-span from the root.
fields.label: Slat span end

fields.help: Trailing-edge flap chord as a fraction of local wing chord.
fields.label: Flap chord fraction

fields.help: Inboard end of the flap run (just outside the fuselage), as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Flap span start

fields.help: Outboard end of the flap run, as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Flap span end

fields.help: Aileron chord as a fraction of local wing chord.
fields.label: Aileron chord fraction

fields.help: Inboard end of the aileron run, as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Aileron span start

fields.help: Outboard end of the aileron run, as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Aileron span end

fields.help: Chord of the inboard (high-speed) aileron or flaperon as a fraction of local wing chord. Zero means the aircraft has none.
fields.label: Inboard aileron chord fraction

fields.help: Inboard end of the inboard aileron run, as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Inboard aileron span start

fields.help: Outboard end of the inboard aileron run, as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Inboard aileron span end

fields.help: Spoiler/speedbrake chord as a fraction of local wing chord (ahead of the flaps).
fields.label: Spoiler chord fraction

fields.help: Inboard end of the spoiler run, as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Spoiler span start

fields.help: Outboard end of the spoiler run (typically spanning the flap run), as a fraction of wing semi-span.
fields.label: Spoiler span end

fields.help: Elevator chord as a fraction of local horizontal-stabilizer chord.
fields.label: Elevator chord fraction

fields.help: Inboard end of the elevator run, as a fraction of h-stab semi-span.
fields.label: Elevator span start

fields.help: Outboard end of the elevator run, as a fraction of h-stab semi-span.
fields.label: Elevator span end

fields.help: Rudder chord as a fraction of local vertical-stabilizer chord.
fields.label: Rudder chord fraction

fields.help: Root-ward end of the rudder run, as a fraction of v-stab span.
fields.label: Rudder span start

fields.help: Tip-ward end of the rudder run, as a fraction of v-stab span.
fields.label: Rudder span end

fields.help: Largest rudder deflection each way [deg]. With rudder chord and span it sets the authority for the one-engine-inoperative yaw balance.
fields.label: Rudder maximum deflection

fields.help: Overall core compression ratio for the free-turbine design cycle. The default is a conceptual design assumption, not certified engine data.
fields.label: Turboprop design pressure ratio

fields.help: Combustor-exit total temperature of the free-turbine design cycle [K].
fields.label: Turboprop design turbine inlet temperature

fields.help: Total-pressure recovery through the inlet (ram + duct losses). Matches the mission inlet_nozzle.pressure_ratio convention.
fields.label: Inlet pressure recovery

fields.help: Fixed low-pressure-compressor (booster) pressure ratio; the high-pressure compressor supplies the rest of the overall pressure ratio (HPC = OPR / this).
fields.label: LPC pressure-ratio split

fields.help: Polytropic (small-stage) compression efficiency of the low-pressure compressor. Lower values cost work at every stage and show up as higher fuel burn.
fields.label: LPC polytropic efficiency

fields.help: Polytropic (small-stage) compression efficiency of the high-pressure compressor.
fields.label: HPC polytropic efficiency

fields.help: Polytropic compression efficiency of the fan, which sets most of the thrust on a high-bypass engine and so matters more here than either compressor.
fields.label: Fan polytropic efficiency

fields.help: Total-pressure loss fraction across the combustor.
fields.label: Combustor pressure ratio

fields.help: Fraction of the fuel's heating value actually released as heat in the combustor.
fields.label: Combustor efficiency

fields.help: Polytropic (small-stage) expansion efficiency of the high-pressure turbine, which drives the high-pressure compressor.
fields.label: HPT polytropic efficiency

fields.help: Polytropic (small-stage) expansion efficiency of the low-pressure turbine, which drives the fan and the booster.
fields.label: LPT polytropic efficiency

fields.help: Shaft power-transmission efficiency for both spools (HPT-HPC, LPT-LPC+fan).
fields.label: Turbine mechanical efficiency

fields.help: Total pressure retained across the core exhaust nozzle.
fields.label: Core nozzle pressure ratio

fields.help: Total pressure retained across the fan (bypass) exhaust nozzle.
fields.label: Fan nozzle pressure ratio

fields.help: Polytropic expansion efficiency of the core exhaust nozzle.
fields.label: Core nozzle efficiency

fields.help: Polytropic expansion efficiency of the fan (bypass) nozzle.
fields.label: Fan nozzle efficiency

fields.help: Lower heating value of Jet-A/Jet-A1 fuel.
fields.label: Fuel heating value

fields.help: Air-standard specific heat used for the inlet/fan/compressor (unburned-air) stations.
fields.label: Cold-section specific heat (cp)

fields.help: Ratio of specific heats for the unburned-air stations, which sets how temperature rises with pressure through the inlet, fan and compressors.
fields.label: Cold-section ratio of specific heats

fields.help: Combustion-gas specific heat used for the combustor/turbine/core-nozzle stations.
fields.label: Hot-section specific heat (cp)

fields.help: Ratio of specific heats for the combustion-gas stations. Lower than the cold-section value because the burned gas is hotter and its molecules have more ways to store energy.
fields.label: Hot-section ratio of specific heats

fields.help: Size a generic wingbox for the optimized wing, write NASTRAN .bdf files and compute theoretical deformations, stresses and frequencies in a normal Run.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.help: Chordwise position of each spar as a fraction of local chord (0 leading edge, 1 trailing edge), one entry per spar in any order.
fields.label: Spar chord positions

fields.help: Which ribs get trailing-edge panels to prevent TE buckling: 'all', 'none', 'alternate', 'inboard', 'outboard', or 'step_N' (every Nth rib).
fields.label: Trailing-edge rib panel mode

fields.help: Adds an optional third spar from the root to the wing break, at center_spar_chord_fraction of chord: partial-span reinforcement where root load is highest.
fields.label: Add center spar (root-to-kink)

fields.help: Chordwise position of the optional center spar (see center_spar_enabled), as a fraction of local chord. Only used when center_spar_enabled is True.
fields.label: Center spar chord position

fields.help: Material name from the built-in structural material database, used for the wing skin panels.
fields.label: Skin material

fields.help: Material for the spar shear webs.
fields.label: Spar web material

fields.help: Material for the spar caps (the primary bending-load-carrying members).
fields.label: Spar cap material

fields.help: Material for the rib webs.
fields.label: Rib material

fields.help: Extra margin multiplied onto the design loads on top of the CS-25 ultimate load factors (dimensionless). 1.0 means no extra margin beyond CS-25 ultimate.
fields.label: Additional safety factor

fields.help: Maximum relative curvature error from neglecting beam rotation, (1 + slope^2)^1.5 - 1.
fields.label: Linear beam curvature error budget

fields.help: Largest tensile stress of the lower wing cover in 1 g flight, set by service life [Pa].
fields.label: Lower-cover fatigue stress limit (1 g)

fields.help: Wing skin thickness actually used [m]. 6 mm matches a large long-range wing.
fields.label: Skin gauge

fields.help: Floor on spar web thickness [m]. The web is sized for shear, which for a large wing falls below what can be manufactured, so this floor usually sets it.
fields.label: Minimum spar web gauge

fields.help: Thickness of every rib web. Ribs carry no bending, so this is a fixed practical gauge rather than a sized quantity.
fields.label: Rib web thickness

fields.help: Thickness of the panel running from the rear spar to the trailing edge on those ribs that carry one.
fields.label: Trailing-edge strip thickness

fields.help: Spanwise fraction below which spar caps keep their full root section (bending is highest inboard).
fields.label: Cap taper lock station

fields.help: Fraction of the locked-section cap flange width/thickness remaining at the wingtip.
fields.label: Cap taper tip fraction

fields.help: Empirical panel-buckling coefficient in the Euler skin-panel critical stress used to derive rib spacing (dimensionless): higher allows wider rib spacing.
fields.label: Rib spacing buckling coefficient

fields.help: Effective radius of gyration of a skin panel stiffened by a stringer, used by the same rib-spacing buckling formula.
fields.label: Stiffened-panel radius of gyration

fields.help: Force an exact number of ribs instead of the auto-derived panel-buckling spacing. Leave blank to let the app determine rib count/spacing.
fields.label: Rib count override

fields.help: Number of spanwise points for load, moment and deflection integration, wing-mass centroid integration and the analytical stress solver. Higher is smoother but slower.
fields.label: Spanwise integration stations

fields.help: Number of chordwise points sampled per rib cross-section in the FEM mesh.
fields.label: Mesh chordwise points per rib

fields.help: Path to nastran.exe (absolute or repo-relative). Blank only writes .bdf files and uses the analytical estimates; no NASTRAN install is needed.
fields.label: NASTRAN executable path

fields.help: Optional absolute path to MSC analysis.exe, passed to the NASTRAN launcher as the a.solver keyword. Leave blank when the launcher finds its own solver.
fields.label: MSC NASTRAN solver override

fields.help: Directory with build/bin/nastran and rf/NASINFO for the local NASA NASTRAN-95 adapter, independent of MSC NASTRAN.
fields.label: Local NASTRAN-95 directory

fields.help: Optional directory containing libgfortran and companion runtime DLLs for local NASTRAN-95. Leave blank when the runtime is already on PATH.
fields.label: NASTRAN-95 runtime directory

fields.help: Optional short absolute directory used to stage local NASTRAN-95 rf files. The 1970s RFOPEN loader accepts at most 37 bytes here; C:/nas-rf is suitable on Windows.
fields.label: NASTRAN-95 RF staging directory

fields.help: Optional NASTRAN-95 OCMEM allocation in words.
fields.label: NASTRAN-95 open-core words

fields.help: Actually invoke nastran_exe_path on the generated .bdf files.
fields.label: Run NASTRAN

fields.help: Pull-up / push-down / 1g-level static load cases -> deformation and stress.
fields.label: Run static analysis (SOL 101)

fields.help: Natural frequencies and mode shapes.
fields.label: Run normal modes (SOL 103)

fields.help: Modal frequency response to a harmonic engine-mounted excitation force.
fields.label: Run sine sweep (SOL 111)

fields.help: Integrate the solved unit-force SOL 111 response against the one-sided force PSD below, giving displacement RMS [m] over the frequency sweep.
fields.label: Calculate random-vibration RMS from SOL 111

fields.help: Max time allowed for one NASTRAN solution (SOL 101/103/111 each run separately) before it's killed.
fields.label: NASTRAN timeout per solution

fields.help: Estimate each solve's memory within this ceiling. Limits concurrent solvers instead of letting every process reserve half the host RAM. Increase for larger meshes.
fields.label: MSC Nastran memory ceiling

fields.help: Max structural modes for SOL 103's EIGRL and the analytical Rayleigh-quotient estimate.
fields.label: Number of modes to extract

fields.help: Highest frequency the sine sweep excites. Above the last mode of interest there is nothing left to find, and every extra step costs a solve.
fields.label: Frequency sweep upper limit

fields.help: Spacing between sweep frequencies. A step coarser than a mode's half-power bandwidth steps over the resonance without seeing it.
fields.label: Frequency sweep step

fields.help: Structural damping assumed for the sine/random vibration response (2% is a common metallic-airframe assumption).
fields.label: Modal damping ratio

fields.help: One-sided flat force PSD at the engine excitation grid [N^2/Hz].
fields.label: Random excitation force PSD

fields.help: Frozen-reference acceleration PSD retained for saved-file compatibility. It is not used by the product RMS path, which requires the force PSD above.
fields.label: Legacy random vibration base PSD (not used)

fields.help: Path (repo-root-relative or absolute) to patran.exe. Leave blank to skip, no Patran install is required for anything else in Structural Analysis. Set on Workspace > External Tools.
fields.label: Patran executable path

fields.help: After a successful SOL 101 static solve, replay a Patran session per load case to export a deformation-plot PNG.
fields.label: Render Patran deformation plots

fields.help: Write the optimized aircraft as an inspectable OpenVSP script and, if OpenVSP is configured, its .vsp3 project and CAD preview.
fields.label: OpenVSP geometry export

fields.help: Run OpenVSP's VSPAERO vortex-lattice comparison on the exported geometry.
fields.label: VSPAERO analysis

fields.help: Run Athena Vortex Lattice's independent take-off comparison and keep its SI deck. The Aerodynamic results selector must include AVL.
fields.label: AVL comparison

fields.help: Run the FLOWUnsteady adapter on the optimized aircraft and keep its request, result and solver logs. Set ALAS_FLOWUNSTEADY_EXE to a compatible executable first.
fields.label: FLOWUnsteady analysis

fields.help: Operating rule that splits fuel on board into taxi, trip, contingency, alternate, final reserve, additional, extra and discretionary fuel.
fields.label: Fuel scheme

fields.help: On: fly the route at the takeoff mass the fuel policy requires, within mass and tank limits, and check the reserves.
fields.label: Fly the policy load case

fields.help: Ground time at idle fuel flow before takeoff [min]; the ramp mass carries it above the takeoff mass. 10-15 min is representative of a large hub.
fields.label: Taxi time

fields.help: Contingency fuel as a fraction of planned trip fuel. EASA basic 0.05 (0.03 with an en-route alternate); FAA flag rule 0.10 of flight time; domestic none.
fields.label: Contingency trip-fuel fraction

fields.help: Minimum contingency fuel as holding time over the destination at the estimated landing mass [min]. EASA basic requires at least 5 min; zero removes the floor.
fields.label: Contingency holding floor

fields.help: Still-air distance from destination to alternate aerodrome after a missed approach [nmi].
fields.label: Alternate distance

fields.help: Holding time over the alternate (or destination) at the estimated landing mass [min]. 30 min is the EASA basic and FAA flag value; FAA domestic uses 45 min.
fields.label: Final reserve hold

fields.help: Flight time at normal cruise consumption carried after the alternate, 14 CFR 121.639 [min]. 45 min is the rule; read only for the FAA domestic scheme.
fields.label: Domestic cruise reserve

fields.help: Fraction of total flight time to the destination carried as reserve fuel, 14 CFR 121.645(b). 0.10 is the rule; read only for the FAA flag/supplemental scheme.
fields.label: Flag flight-time fraction

fields.help: Height above aerodrome elevation at which contingency and final-reserve holding fuel is evaluated. Every scheme here states 1,500 ft in standard conditions.
fields.label: Holding altitude above aerodrome

fields.help: Fuel for specific cases the general reserves do not cover, such as engine failure or depressurisation on an extended-diversion route [kg]. Zero unless studied.
fields.label: Additional fuel

fields.help: Fuel added above the planned requirement, either for anticipated delays (extra) or at the commander's discretion. It is carried and burned last, so it only raises the takeoff mass.
fields.label: Extra and discretionary fuel

fields.help: Share of every tank's geometric volume that cannot be filled, held for thermal expansion of the fuel. CS 25.969 and 14 CFR 25.969 require at least two percent of the tank capacity.
fields.label: Expansion space fraction

fields.help: Fraction of usable tank capacity left undeliverable in the most adverse feed condition. CS 25.959 requires test; 0.005-0.01 is typical. Counts as operating empty mass.
fields.label: Unusable fuel fraction

fields.help: Whether this wing tank exists on the aircraft. A tank that is not installed contributes no capacity, no centroid and no unusable fuel.
fields.label: Installed

fields.help: Inboard boundary of the tank as a fraction of the semi-span from the centreline [0-1].
fields.label: Span start

fields.help: Outboard boundary of the tank as a fraction of the semi-span. Transport wing tanks end short of the tip, leaving the outer bays dry for the ailerons and the surge tank.
fields.label: Span end

fields.help: Fraction of the geometric spar-box volume between the two stations that is usable tank volume (dimensionless), after ribs, systems and expansion space. 0.90-0.95 is typical.
fields.label: Usable volume fraction

fields.help: Order in which the tank is used in normal operation; lower numbers first.
fields.label: Burn priority

fields.help: Manufacturer's published usable volume for this tank, both sides together [L]. When set it is the authoritative capacity; the geometry only supplies the centroid.
fields.label: Published usable volume

fields.help: Whether part of this wing cell is an engine feed tank, kept as a separate tank for the fill and burn sequence.
fields.label: Installed

fields.help: Inboard boundary of the feed tank as a fraction of the semi-span. The feed tank must lie inside its host cell and share one of its ends.
fields.label: Span start

fields.help: Outboard boundary of the feed tank as a fraction of the semi-span. The feed tank must lie inside its host cell and share one of its ends.
fields.label: Span end

fields.label: Published usable volume

fields.help: Whether the wing carry-through box under the cabin floor is a fuel tank. Most transports have one; some short-range variants leave it dry.
fields.label: Installed

fields.help: Fraction of the carry-through spar-box volume between the body sides that is usable tank volume (dimensionless). Lower than a wing tank: keel, gear and systems cross it.
fields.label: Usable volume fraction

fields.help: Order in which the centre tank is used; lower numbers first.
fields.label: Burn priority

fields.help: Manufacturer's published usable volume for the centre tank [L]. When set it is the authoritative capacity; the geometry only supplies the centroid.
fields.label: Published usable volume

fields.help: Whether the horizontal stabiliser box is a fuel tank. Long-range Airbus types use one to hold the cruise centre of gravity aft and cut trim drag; most twins do not have one.
fields.label: Installed

fields.help: Share of the geometric stabiliser spar-box volume between the two stations that is usable tank volume.
fields.label: Usable volume fraction

fields.help: Inboard boundary of the trim tank as a fraction of the stabiliser semi-span from the aircraft centreline.
fields.label: Span start

fields.help: Outboard boundary of the trim tank as a fraction of the stabiliser semi-span.
fields.label: Span end

fields.help: Order in which the trim tank is consumed: lower numbers are used first. In service it is transferred forward late in cruise so the aircraft lands with it empty.
fields.label: Burn priority

fields.help: Usable volume published by the manufacturer for the trim tank. When set it is the authoritative capacity and the geometric estimate only supplies the centroid.
fields.label: Published usable volume

fields.help: Sustained pump rate moving trim fuel between the trim tank and the feed tanks [kg/s], from manufacturer data.
fields.label: Trim transfer rate

fields.help: Whether a fuselage auxiliary tank is installed, such as the Learjet 60 fuselage tank or an extra tank in the cargo hold. Its capacity is a declared volume.
fields.label: Installed

fields.help: Usable volume of the auxiliary tank. It is a declared quantity rather than a geometric estimate.
fields.label: Usable volume

fields.help: Centroid of the auxiliary tank as a fraction of fuselage length from the nose [0-1].
fields.label: Longitudinal position

fields.help: Order in which the auxiliary tank is consumed: lower numbers are used first. Fuselage fuel is transferred into the wing tanks early in cruise.
fields.label: Burn priority

fields.help: For a preset with a published total usable volume, scale every geometric tank estimate by one common factor to reproduce it.
fields.label: Calibrate geometry to published capacity
